The One Trip to Take in Every Decade of Your Life

Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 0:00 Instaread
Sponsored by

If you’ve been waiting for retirement to take that trip of a lifetime, you may want to consider adding a few more vacations to your bucket list. After all, life is long, and some excursions only get better with age. From riding the Shinkansen across Japan to spotting wildlife on a safari in South Africa, here’s the one trip to take in every decade of your life.

Twenties - Backpacking Across Europe

Your twenties are made for Europe: a time to pick up new interests, meet people from every background and soak up history. A Eurail Global Pass covers 33 countries, and FlixBus and Ryanair keep fares low.

Pack one big bag, bed down in hostels or on a sleeper train, and accept a little discomfort while you are young enough to enjoy it, from London’s Camden Market to paragliding in Interlaken and live music at Dublin’s Temple Bar.

Thirties - Japan

Next, try a new continent. Japan is a welcoming first step into Asia: it takes more research, everyday tasks like ordering a meal feel new again, and a growing expat community means more English is spoken.

See Tokyo’s Harajuku and Tokyo Tower, take the Shinkansen to Osaka, Kyoto and Hiroshima for Osaka Castle and Kinkaku-ji Temple, then finish in Hakone with Mount Fuji views, an onsen and a night in a ryokan.

Forties - Peru and Bolivia

Kids and bigger jobs make long getaways harder in your forties, so set aside time for a trek through Peru and Bolivia.

Reach Machu Picchu from Cusco by train or the Inca Trail, explore Lima and the Sacred Valley, then fly to La Paz, the world’s highest capital, and on to the huge Salar de Uyuni salt flat.

Fifties - Iceland

Iceland makes a restful yet lively trip in your fifties, and one week covers a lot. Winter means warm layers but better odds of the northern lights, plus ice caves, the Blue Lagoon and Jökulsárlón lagoon.

Summer brings puffins, green hills, Goðafoss, the geysers at Geysir and the black sand of Reynisfjara.

Sixties - South Africa

Mark your 60th in Africa: look for the Big Five in Kruger National Park, then head to Cape Town for wine tasting, the cableway up Table Mountain and the Kirstenbosch botanical garden.

Seventies - Danube River Cruise

Celebrate retirement at 70 with a Danube cruise on Viking, Avalon Waterways or Uniworld, moving slowly from Hungary to Germany with meals and outings arranged, plus optional tours, hotel nights and tastings.

Eighties: Rocky Mountaineer Train, Canada

In your eighties, an easy scenic train ride can replace a long flight. The Rocky Mountaineer’s First Passage to the West crosses the Continental Divide from Banff to Vancouver, stopping at Lake Louise and Kamloops on one of Canada’s earliest western rail routes.

Marissa Kozma | Writer
